segments.t: Fedya plays a prank on Senya, making him yell that he is on fire. When Lyova rushes over to help, he feels the bottle of oil strapped to Senya's leg. Listen to the full conversation in Russian first, and then we will walk through every line together.
Ой, горю, горю, горю!
Ребята, помогите мне, помогите!
Что это у тебя такое твёрдое?
А это совсем не твоё дело.
А ну, быстро стой здесь.
Это что ещё у тебя такое?
Лёва, это вообще не моё.
Правда, это совсем не твоё?
Нет, конечно, это не моё.
Ну да, конечно, я так и поверил.
Я буду тебя персонально обыскивать.
В конце каждого рабочего дня.

'Guys, help me, help!' Senya brings out the contrast between 'guys' and 'help' in a few short words.

'What is that hard thing you have there?' The grammar packs 'what' and 'hard' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.

'That is none of your business at all.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'and' and finishing on 'business'. Lyova answers right away.

'Come on, stand right here quickly.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'and' and finishing on 'here'.

'What else is this that you have?' Lyova raises the pitch on 'such' to turn the phrase into a direct spoken question.
Лёва, это вообще не моё.
'Lyova, this is not mine at all.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'Lyova' before landing on 'my'. Lyova answers right away.
Правда, это совсем не твоё?
'Really, this is not yours at all?' The grammar packs 'really' and 'your' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Нет, конечно, это не моё.
'No, of course, this is not mine.' Senya anchors the line on 'no', while 'my' completes the thought.
Ну да, конечно, я так и поверил.
'Well yes, of course, as if I believed that.' The '-l' ending on the verb meaning 'to believe' places the action in the masculine past tense.
Я буду тебя персонально обыскивать.
'I will search you personally.' Lyova brings out the contrast between 'I' and 'will be' in a few short words.
В конце каждого рабочего дня.
'At the end of every working day.' In Russian, the idea of 'end' flows naturally into 'day' without extra filler words. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
